THE TWO FAILURE CLASSES AND HOW THEY ARE COMPUTED (I reverse-engineered these from scripts/notes_content.py; trust them):

1. "FAIL description in key_concept" - a key_concept bullet repeats the description. The checker splits `description` into clauses (on sentence ends, " - ", and "; ") and flags any key_concept bullet that CONTAINS one of those clauses verbatim (case/whitespace-insensitive), or is contained in one. FIX: reword the offending bullet so no description clause survives inside it, and give the bullet a genuinely different angle. Do NOT delete a "Level N:" bullet - these notes carry a Level 1 to Level 5 ladder and the ladder must stay intact with all its levels.

2. "FAIL shareable_thought[N] not from principle" - each shareable line must echo the note's own principle text. The allowed pool = the whole `description`, the whole flattened `key_concept`, and every clause of them (split on sentence ends, " - ", "; "). A line passes when, after lowercasing and whitespace-normalizing, it either IS a substring of a pool entry or CONTAINS a pool entry of at least 10 characters. EASIEST RELIABLE FIX: make the shareable line a contiguous span of existing description/key_concept wording (you may capitalize the first letter and end it with a period). If the existing wording does not stand alone well, edit the key_concept bullet AND the shareable line together so the span reads well in both places.

HARD CONSTRAINTS the linters enforce (violating any of these creates a NEW failure):
- shareable_thought: exactly 4 items, each <= 130 chars, no "[[wikilinks]]", must NOT start with not/and/or/but/then, must end with "." "!" or "?", at least 5 words, and no line may be a prefix or suffix of another line (that trips an overlap check). Four different angles: definition, move, boundary, payoff.
- description: third person, <= 20 words, no "[[wikilinks]]", and no standalone word "I".
- examples: exactly 2 items, one sentence each - the linter counts [.!?] characters and allows only ONE per example, so avoid "a.m.", "e.g.", "U.S." and decimals.
- No contractions (don't, it's, can't...) anywhere in description, key_concept, examples, shareable_thought.
- No em dashes or en dashes anywhere - use a plain hyphen "-".
- key_concept line 1 (the first non-shortcode line) must not contain a wikilink.

VOICE (the point of the exercise, not just passing lint): plain words a person would say out loud, first person where natural in examples and faith glosses, concrete scenes with friction rather than ideal cases. Faith notes must stay in the free grace tradition (faith alone for eternal life; works for discipleship and rewards, never merit) and keep a straight tone in verse commentary - no dry humor there.

One thing worth knowing for the rest of this batch: the clause splitter's character class spans `-` through `–`, so it also splits on any single character between spaces. That is why description tails like "a guessing game" and "a saved link is" become their own clauses and trip the check in places that look harmless.
